selected_mathematical_checks: The full source localization theorem is uniform in both mismatch counts, one-qubit reference vectors and uncounted registers. The inverse circuit stays at the same reflection depth. Taking U=C* and the output-zero product projection gives the conjugated observable used here without a coherent-output reduction or extra gates.

For biased one-site vectors v=(sqrt(1-p),sqrt(p)) and w=(sqrt(p),-sqrt(1-p)), w(x)v(x) equals the product probability times (p-x)/sqrt(p(1-p)). Averaging simultaneous Z phases on the bra and ket removes every off-diagonal matrix term. The nonempty-subset constant contribution vanishes. Orthonormality, Jensen and Bessel give the factor four times the squared localization norm.

Uniformity in the reference vectors pays biases approaching zero or one. Deterministic coordinates are restrictions/limits. Conditional circuit restrictions retain the physical total N and all original resource bounds. Product Fourier diagonalization gives the exact heat-bath conditional-variance Dirichlet form, with rate one per site rather than one update per whole system.

Conditioning on the complement of an independent color class leaves independent spins with arbitrary effective fields. Summing conditional site variances in that class and then averaging gives exactly the corresponding physical Ising energy. Summing q classes gives qk+4n exp(-2N^s), with no coupling-strength or mixing hypothesis.

A=J+aI is positive semidefinite and its diagonal is a. The Gaussian moment-generating identity, including a singular covariance by a limit, yields the stated cosh-weighted product mixture; diagonal shifting changes the Ising Hamiltonian only by a constant. All finite-dimensional integrals exist at arbitrary finite fields.

For fixed outside spins eta, Gaussian linear tilting gives theta mean b=h_i+sum_(j!=i)J_ij eta_j and variance a before the cosh tilt. The posterior normalization is exp(a/2)cosh b. Averaged product conditional variance and physical conditional variance therefore have the exact ratio r_a(b) displayed in (G), including its factor exp(-a/2).

The inequality cosh(b+u)<=cosh(b)exp(|u|) followed by Jensen gives r_a(b)>=exp(-a/2-sqrt(2a/pi)). Conditional variance decomposition gives r_a(b)<=1. Integrating the product energy uses the lower comparison, so the inverse factor in (B) has the correct orientation. A product-mixture representation alone would not prove it.

Self-adjoint heat-bath evolution gives NS_u(f)=2<f,(I-P_u)f> and bounds it by 2u D(f). With delta=min(epsilon/2,1/2), t=delta/(2c), s=delta/(4c), the chosen k dominates N^t and the error decays uniformly. The statement concerns expected measured sign, not disagreements of fresh independent measurements.

The correlation interface uses reversibility, ||f||_2<=1 and (1-e^(-v))^2<=2(1-e^(-v)). The target autocorrelation includes its squared mean; centered covariance alone is not enough for a 1/2 success conclusion. The stationary-pair triangle bound has denominator eight, since ||f-g||_2^2<=2(1-<f,g>).

The disjoint-edge density formula has exact second moment (1+t^2)^(n/2) and maximum (1+t)^(n/2). It is a counterexample to a dimension-free density-comparison shortcut, not to either proved circuit-energy estimate.
